newsitem.title: UK: Bonds power on, but chartists see risk of fatigue.
newsitem.headline: Bonds power on, but chartists see risk of fatigue.

text.p: European bond futures, basking in the glow from soaring Treasuries, must set new record highs to abort the risk of a sell-off, technical analysts said on Wednesday.
Expectations that U.S. interest rates would not rise imminently pushed French and German futures through contract highs, but looming overhead is formidable resistance from all-time highs.
"We could be seeing the last moves up before a major move down," said Howard Friend, Elliott Wave analyst at MCM YieldWatch in London. "I won't be bullish unless those highs are taken out."
Although BTPs are breaking into new territory, the notionnel has yet to overcome the all-time high on continuation charts at 132.94 set on February 18 1997, and Bunds face 104.04 set the same day.
September notionnel futures were up 0.28 at 130.98 by 1100 GMT, after reaching a contract high of 131.24 in early trade. Bunds were up 21 at 103.24, after a new contract high of 103.52.

"You have to be very careful up here," said David Wood, an independent technical analyst near London. "European markets are relying heavily on the U.S. If the U.S. didn't exist, you'd be taking out puts up against all the highs."

Analysts said one of the main technical spurs had been the break above the "massive" technical level at 115-17 on the T-bond futures. The September contract set a peak of 115-17 on December 3 1996, before declining to a low of 105-30 in April 1997.
Wood said T-bonds must spend some time consolidating above 115-00 to give European markets a chance to gun down the record levels.
"If we assume that's possible, then Bunds can fulfil their potential to set new highs," he said. "A projection of the rally from September gives a target of 104.81."
But Friend said Bunds have broken down from the 104.04 level in five waves, basing at the 99.05 low in April, and moves since then were an abc pattern.
Elliott theory holds that markets trend in a five wave pattern, followed by a three wave corrections labelled a-b-c.
Friend said the c wave could top out in the mid 103.00s, or 103.77, leaving Bunds set for a "big move down, perhaps to the high 100.00s to start with."
He said T-bonds were in the same boat, and were likely to top out juste under the 116-00 level.
Anil Patel, technical analyst at Nomura International in London, said it was crucial for the notionnel to hold its break above 130.88 high on a closing basis.
"I would welcome a correction, but overall the record highs are under threat," he said.
And although gilts have been somewhat left behind by the bond market bonhomie, he said the futures would hit 118-119 by the year end.
"I can easily see gilts rallying two to three points in a couple of day's trading," he said.
September gilt futures set a contract high well below this decade's highs in December 1993 at 121-06.
But impulsive spikes have to backed up by solid price action to confirm the move, analysts said.
"Sharp moves up like we've seen, with low, or no, real volume are typical of tops," said Friend.
